title: Empirical Risk Minimization
interviewAnswer: ERM minimizes average training loss; generalization theory asks when low empirical risk also implies low expected risk on unseen data.
why: ERM is the abstraction behind most supervised objectives.
intuition: Training optimizes the sample you have, but deployment cares about an unknown population.
deepDive: Population risk is an expectation over the data distribution; empirical risk replaces it with a sample average. Capacity, sample size and sampling assumptions affect the gap.
commonMistakes: Equating training loss with true risk.
Assuming ERM guarantees a global optimum for nonconvex networks.
production: Validation must represent deployment; theory cannot fix a mismatched sampling process.
workedExample: A deep tree can drive training risk near zero while test risk worsens.
